title: Counter-Selector Wave 32: candidate handoff-ladder application
purpose: Apply the public authority-transfer and recipient-acknowledgment controls to the strongest living and historical candidate lanes. Add a bounded person-level custody observation only where a named recipient acknowledges receiving a bounded project object and successor operation is independently visible, while preserving the difference between incoming stewardship and a complete outgoing handoff.

bounded_person_custody_may_be_supported_: a named person receives an entrusted object or role
the received object is sufficiently bounded to inspect
the person demonstrably preserves or advances the object
the claim remains scoped to the observed custody event
missing package, credential, rollback, and external-review receipts remain explicit
complete_direct_handoff_requires: attributable recipient acknowledgment of the package rather than only the role or meeting
authority, credentials, dependencies, and open decisions inventoried
rollback, refusal, and safe-decline conditions preserved
successor action observed from the transferred state
continuity observed without hidden focal-person state

candidate_lanes.public_label: historical recipient-side maintainer transfer and successor releases

source_records.title: How curl Became Like This
source_records.artifact_scope: Records Rafael Sagula's httpget 0.1 release, Daniel Stenberg's 0.2 additions, his rapid succession as maintainer, and later releases and renames.

source_records.title: changes from before it was curl
source_records.artifact_scope: States that Rafael Sagula handed over the keys to the kingdom, identifies the inherited object as a single roughly 300-line C file, and records subsequent releases.

source_records.title: Changes in 0.1
source_records.artifact_scope: Preserves the original httpget 0.1 release date and establishes the pre-handover object.

source_records.title: Changes in 0.2
source_records.artifact_scope: Preserves the first release after Daniel's additions while also recording that the detailed changes are lost.

source_records.title: curl versions
source_records.artifact_scope: Preserves the 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1.0, and later release dates across the maintained project lineage.

source_records.title: curl project governance
source_records.artifact_scope: Shows current lead and infrastructure authority concentration, backup roles, maintainers, and the absence of an observed successor release authority.

review.artifact_validity_position: A named recipient acknowledges receiving maintainer control of a bounded code object and then demonstrably releases and advances it.
review.adversarial_position: The account is retrospective and first-party; the actual package, credentials, decisions, dependencies, and rollback state are not preserved, and current authority remains concentrated.

counterevidence: The handover account is retrospective and authored by the recipient.
The actual outgoing package, credential transfer, and recipient receipt are not preserved.
The detailed changes for releases 0.2 and 1.0 are recorded as lost.
No complete open-decision, dependency, rollback, or safe-decline inventory was located.
Current release and infrastructure authority remains heavily concentrated in the same person.
Successful incoming stewardship does not prove an outgoing handoff that another operator can repeat.
falsifiers: evidence that Rafael Sagula did not transfer maintainership
evidence that Daniel did not produce the successor releases
evidence that the 0.2 lineage was unrelated to the 0.1 object
a public complete package and acknowledgment that would justify a stronger direct-handoff state
independent review rejecting the bounded custody interpretation

candidate_lanes.public_label: founder-independent framework continuation under community governance

source_records.title: Django FAQ: General
source_records.artifact_scope: Identifies the original co-creators and the project's open-source lineage.

source_records.title: Django governance update
source_records.artifact_scope: Preserves the transition away from the former BDFL structure into collective governance.

source_records.title: Django Software Foundation teams
source_records.artifact_scope: Lists current teams and roles that govern, merge, release, and sustain the project.

source_records.title: Django release process
source_records.artifact_scope: Documents the current collective release process and the project state available to current operators.

review.artifact_validity_position: The project demonstrably continues under community governance without the focal co-creator governing it.
review.adversarial_position: The outgoing package, recipient, credentials, decisions, and transition action attributable to the focal person are not isolated.

counterevidence: Collective continuation does not identify a focal-person outgoing package.
Current governance and release process may have evolved after the focal person ceased governing.
No recipient acknowledgment of a focal-person package was located.
Community continuity cannot be assigned as sole person custody.
falsifiers: a Simon-authored outgoing state package with named recipient
recipient acknowledgment of the package and credentials
evidence that current operation still depends on hidden Simon-only state
independent review supporting or rejecting person custody

candidate_lanes.public_label: sensitive-service sustainability redesign and team expansion

source_records.title: I'm Open Sourcing the Have I Been Pwned Code Base
source_records.artifact_scope: Identifies sole-person dependency after a failed acquisition process and announces an open-code sustainability route.

source_records.title: Pwned Passwords, Open Source in the .NET Foundation and Working with the FBI
source_records.artifact_scope: Records repositories, foundation and platform assistance, and an intended community-supported operating model.

source_records.title: Have I Been Pwned Employee 1.0: Stefán Jökull Sigurðarson
source_records.artifact_scope: Records the first full-time employee and explicitly discusses the founder's difficulty letting go.

source_records.title: Have I Been Pwned 2.0 is Now Live!
source_records.artifact_scope: Records a large team-supported service rebuild and public release after the sustainability transition.

review.artifact_validity_position: Open code, named collaborators, team expansion, and later service delivery are real continuity artifacts.
review.adversarial_position: The complete sensitive operating state, credentials, queues, breach-data custody, incident state, and authority remain absent from the public surface.

counterevidence: The focal person remains founder and chief public operator.
Open-source components do not contain complete sensitive service state.
No recipient acknowledgment of credentials, data custody, queues, incidents, or rollback state was located.
Later service releases are team outcomes and do not prove a complete outgoing package.
falsifiers: a public full-service runbook and state inventory
recipient acknowledgment of authority and credentials
observed full service operation during focal-person absence
evidence that all sensitive state is reproducible from the public package
independent review supporting or rejecting person custody

source_records.title: Exchange of Letters on the Resignation of the Ambassador at Large and Special Representative for the Law of the Sea Conference
source_records.artifact_scope: Names an experienced continuing delegation, remaining work, and the outgoing operator's offer of future assistance.

source_records.title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1981–1988, Volume XLI, Document 114 footnote 4
source_records.publisher: Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State
source_records.artifact_scope: Preserves continuity and differences between Richardson-era and successor negotiating objectives.

source_records.title: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1981–1988, Volume XLI, Document 119
source_records.publisher: Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State
source_records.artifact_scope: Places Richardson inside the continuing delegation as an expert and advisory committee chair after leadership transition.

review.artifact_validity_position: The outgoing record and successor-era records preserve real institutional continuity and predecessor availability.
review.adversarial_position: No recipient acknowledges a Richardson package, and no files, credentials, decisions, dependencies, or rollback state are inventoried.

counterevidence: The outgoing letter names an experienced delegation but not a state package.
No successor acknowledgment itemizes files, credentials, open decisions, dependencies, or deadlines.
Richardson's continued availability may mask incomplete independent resumability.
Objective continuity is not proof of person-to-person custody.
falsifiers: a direct successor acknowledgment of a Richardson state package
an itemized outgoing file and decision inventory
evidence that successor operation depended on hidden Richardson-only state
independent review supporting or rejecting the existing custody scope

next_action: Expose the Daniel custody addition and the unchanged Simon, Troy, and Richardson handoff states to external artifact review; search for outgoing packages, recipient package receipts, credentials, dependencies, open decisions, rollback conditions, and observed successor operation without contacting source subjects.
